tasks.corrected_reference_answer: NDimArray.__new__ is a convenience factory returning ImmutableDenseNDimArray(iterable, shape, **kwargs), while the base __getitem__ leaves storage access to subclasses (sympy/tensor/array/ndim_array.py:142-147). Thus calling NDimArray does create a concrete array. Delegation supplies a default representation; the source does not establish that another initializer is impossible or that dense storage is universally faster.

tasks.notes: Read the question/reference and relevant pinned-source code; static review only, no repository code executed.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: TensMul._extract_data collects operand arrays, computes dummy contractions and sorts free indices by their positions before contraction (sympy/tensor/tensor.py:4178-4186). _indices_to_free_dum tracks operand and overall index positions explicitly (3492-3536). Therefore arbitrary operand reorderings do not automatically produce identically ordered arrays. For mathematically equivalent expressions, compare arrays using an explicit common free-index order via replace_with_arrays(..., indices), whose contract controls output axes (2279-2292); commutation and symmetry assumptions must also hold.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: No new simplify flag is needed for independent tests: exptrigsimp is already a standalone public function (sympy/simplify/trigsimp.py:571-596), and direct tests include cos(x) +/- I*sin(x) cases (sympy/simplify/tests/test_trigsimp.py:384-403). Test it directly to avoid simplify’s earlier normalization stage. Its final guard rejects a rewritten result that introduces I when the input lacked it (sympy/simplify/trigsimp.py:659-662). Any optional-stage refactor would be a separate design proposal, not required by the current API.
